about: The crate policy Genex ships beside the Rust payload's lock line (owner decision 2026-10-08, option C). A crate an agent requests is added only when the person approves it; the checks below run offline on the approved closure. src/substrate/toolchain-store/crate-policy.ts pins this file's sha256 (CRATE_POLICY_SHA256) and refuses any other bytes (crate-policy-tampered). scripts/toolchains/crate-policy.ts refresh moves the snapshot and rewrites every pin.

advisories.rule: A RustSec advisory of the pinned snapshot against any crate of the closure refuses it (crate-advisory) even when the person approved it, unless the advisory is withdrawn (its author took it back) or is an informational unmaintained notice (no vulnerability: shown in the advisory database, never blocking). Vulnerabilities, informational unsound advisories and informational notices block. cargo-deny applies it as unmaintained = "none", unsound = "all" (it never reports a withdrawn advisory); the built-in rules apply the same table.

licences.rule: Every crate of the closure is under an expression the allow list satisfies, or it is refused (crate-licence).

bans.rule: A banned crate anywhere in the closure refuses it (crate-banned).

audits.rule: cargo-vet reads each trusted source's pinned audit list; the result is shown to the person and never refuses on its own. A source whose sha256 is null is not pinned yet: it is shown as not asked until scripts/toolchains/crate-policy.ts refresh --audits pins it.

approvals.rule: The person's approval is the deciding vote. A closure with a build script or a proc macro also needs the person's separate approval of that kind (crate-build-script, crate-proc-macro); the build sandbox is unchanged.
